title: LCSW Billing: Codes, Payers and the Payer Code Matrix

cards.title: What Can an LCSW Bill, and Who Decides?
cards.content:
A Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW) can bill many mental health codes, but not every code, and not every payer pays for the same ones.

This lesson covers:

• The identifiers that tell a payer you are an LCSW
• Where each payer's list of billable codes actually comes from
• The codes Medicare covers for an LCSW, and the ones an LCSW can never bill
• How to bill so every service you earned gets paid

**Download the LCSW Payer Code Matrix** (Word) with the button below. Its Medicare column is filled in from CMS sources. The other payer columns are blank for you to fill in from your contracts.

cards.title: Two Different IDs: Taxonomy vs. Medicare Specialty Code
cards.content:
People often mix these up.

• **NPI taxonomy code 1041C0700X** (Social Worker, Clinical). This comes from the national NUCC taxonomy code set. It is on your NPI record, and some payers want it on the claim.
• **Medicare specialty code 80**. This is Medicare's own internal label. The CMS Medicare Claims Processing Manual, Chapter 12, §150 says: "CSWs are identified on the provider file by specialty code 80 and provider type 56."

The same section sets two payment rules for Medicare:

• **Payment is 75% of the Physician Fee Schedule.**
• **Assignment is required**, so you must accept Medicare's allowed amount.

visual.title: LCSW IDENTIFIERS
visual.sub: Taxonomy is national; specialty 80 is Medicare's

cards.title: Payers Do Not Hand You One Complete List
cards.content:
What an LCSW can bill comes from three layers, checked together:

• **The code books.** The AMA CPT book and the CMS HCPCS list define each code and its rules (minimum minutes, which add-ons go together).
• **Your state license.** California's Board of Behavioral Sciences sets your scope of practice. No payer can pay you for something outside it.
• **Each payer's rules.** Medicare publishes its rules for everyone (CMS manuals, the Physician Fee Schedule, NCCI edits). Medi-Cal publishes the Medi-Cal Provider Manual and fee schedule, and Partnership HealthPlan adds its own manual and policies. Commercial plans put a **fee schedule exhibit** in the contract, usually only for the codes you ask about, plus reimbursement policies on their portals.

visual.sub: Check all three layers for every code

cards.question: A payer form asks for the LCSW's taxonomy code. Which do you enter?
cards.explanation: 1041C0700X is the NUCC taxonomy code for a clinical social worker. Specialty code 80 and provider type 56 are Medicare's internal provider-file labels (CMS Claims Processing Manual, Ch. 12 §150). 90837 is a CPT code, not an identifier.

visual.hint: One is national (NUCC); one is Medicare-only.

cards.title: Medicare's Rule for What an LCSW Can Bill
cards.content:
The CMS Medicare Benefit Policy Manual, Chapter 15, §170 covers clinical social worker services that are:

• For the **diagnosis and treatment of mental illness**
• Services the CSW is **legally authorized to perform under state law**
• Services **of a type Medicare would cover if a physician furnished them**
• **Not otherwise excluded** from coverage

**Not covered (§170.D):** services to hospital inpatients, and services a skilled nursing facility (SNF) must provide to its own inpatients as a condition of participating in Medicare.

boxes.b: Diagnosis and treatment of mental illness, within state scope.
Would be covered if a physician did it.
Hospital inpatients; SNF services the SNF must provide.
75% of the fee schedule; assignment required.

cards.title: The Core Codes: Evaluation and Psychotherapy
cards.content:
**90791**: psychiatric diagnostic evaluation (the intake), with no medical services.

Individual psychotherapy is **time-based**. The minutes you document decide the code (CPT time ranges; confirm in your current CPT book):

• **90832**: 16–37 minutes
• **90834**: 38–52 minutes
• **90837**: 53 minutes or more

Under 16 minutes, no individual psychotherapy code applies. Record start and stop times every session. Some commercial payers require prior authorization for 90837 or review frequent use, so check each payer's policy.

cards.question: An LCSW documents a 55-minute individual psychotherapy session (start and stop times recorded). Which code fits?
cards.explanation: 53 minutes or more is 90837. Billing 90834 for a 55-minute session leaves earned payment unpaid; billing 90837 for a 45-minute session would be upcoding.

visual.hint: Find the range that includes 55 minutes.

cards.title: Add-Ons and Crisis Codes
cards.content:
**+90785, interactive complexity** (add-on, never billed alone). Use it only when a documented factor made communication harder, for example a parent in conflict or a caregiver who interferes. Per CPT it goes with 90791, the psychotherapy codes and 90853, but **not** with the crisis codes.

**90839, psychotherapy for crisis, first 60 minutes.** Bill for 30–74 minutes of crisis care. Document the urgent assessment, the crisis history, mental status and the disposition.

**+90840**: each additional 30 minutes of crisis care beyond the first 74.

A real crisis session billed as 90837 is underbilled. A routine session billed as 90839 is not supported.

cards.title: Family and Group Psychotherapy
cards.content:
• **90846**: family psychotherapy **without** the patient present
• **90847**: family psychotherapy **with** the patient present
• **90853**: group psychotherapy (not a family group), billed per patient in the group

For the family codes, the session must focus on the **patient's** treatment, not on another family member's problems.

visual.title: FAMILY AND GROUP
visual.sub: Focus stays on the patient's treatment

cards.title: Newer Medicare Codes LCSWs Can Bill
cards.content:
Medicare opened these to clinical social workers in recent fee schedule rules (per CMS and NASW summaries; verify before billing):

• **Health behavior assessment and intervention (since 2024):** 96156; 96158/+96159 (individual); 96164/+96165 (group); 96167/+96168 (family with patient). These are for psychological and behavioral factors affecting a **physical** health problem, such as coping with chronic pain or diabetes. For treating a mental health diagnosis, use psychotherapy codes.
• **G0323 (since 2023):** general behavioral health integration care management, at least 20 minutes per calendar month, with an initiating visit and patient consent.
• **G0560 (since 2025):** safety planning, per 20 minutes, personally performed.
• **G0544 (since 2025):** a monthly bundle of 4 follow-up calls after an ED or hospital discharge for a crisis.

visual.title: NEWER MEDICARE CODES
visual.sub: Bill only when the service truly fits

boxes.b: BHI care management, 20+ min a month.

cards.question: An LCSW sees a Medicare patient to help them cope with the stress of managing newly diagnosed diabetes. The patient has no mental health diagnosis. Which code family fits best?
cards.explanation: Health behavior assessment and intervention codes address psychological and behavioral factors affecting a physical health condition. Medicare opened them to clinical social workers in 2024. Office visit codes and 90792 are not billable by an LCSW, and psychotherapy codes are for treating a mental health diagnosis.

visual.hint: The problem is coping with diabetes, not a mental illness.

cards.title: Codes an LCSW Cannot Bill
cards.content:
• **99202–99215** office/outpatient evaluation and management (E/M) visits: these are for practitioners who furnish medical services.
• **90792**: diagnostic evaluation **with medical services**. LCSWs use 90791.
• **+90833, +90836, +90838**: psychotherapy add-ons that only attach to an E/M visit, which an LCSW cannot bill.
• **Medication management**: prescribing or managing psychiatric medication is outside an LCSW's scope.

**Could not confirm:** psychological testing (96130 and related codes). Sources disagree on whether a California LCSW can bill them, so check the BBS scope of practice and each payer's policy.

visual.title: NOT BILLABLE BY AN LCSW
visual.sub: Medical services are outside the scope

boxes.b: Add-ons that need an E/M visit.

cards.question: Which code can an LCSW bill for an initial diagnostic evaluation?
cards.explanation: 90791 is the diagnostic evaluation without medical services. 90792 includes medical services, 99204 is an E/M visit, and +90833 is a psychotherapy add-on to an E/M visit; none of those are billable by an LCSW.

visual.hint: Pick the evaluation without medical services.

cards.title: Getting Each Payer's Codes and Rates
cards.content:
**Medicare:** look up each code in the CMS Physician Fee Schedule Look-Up Tool for your California locality, then multiply by 0.75. Check NCCI edits before billing two codes on the same day.

**Medi-Cal / Partnership HealthPlan:** Partnership policy CLPM-28 says the county mental health plan, not Partnership, pays mental health claims billed with certain codes. Get the current code list and LCSW rates in writing from Partnership's provider manual or provider relations.

**Commercial plans:** before you sign, send the payer your code list and ask for the LCSW rate on each code, plus any prior authorization limits and their telehealth place of service and modifier. That is also when you negotiate.

The matrix (download on card 1) includes a request script you can copy.

cards.question: The CMS Physician Fee Schedule tool shows $100.00 for a code in your locality (example number). What does Medicare pay an LCSW for it?
cards.explanation: Medicare pays clinical social workers 75% of the Physician Fee Schedule (Claims Processing Manual, Ch. 12 §150): $100.00 × 0.75 = $75.00. The $100.00 is an example number, not a real rate.

visual.hint: Multiply the fee schedule amount by 0.75.

cards.title: Billing Workflow: Get Paid for Everything You Earned
cards.content:
Bill exactly what you did and documented. Billing a higher code than the documentation supports is upcoding, which is fraud.

**Before the visit**
• Verify eligibility and benefits, including whether behavioral health is carved out to another plan or the county.
• Check prior authorization rules for the code you expect to bill.
• Confirm credentialing, and that your NPI and taxonomy match the payer's records.

**Documentation**
• Start and stop times for every timed code.
• The reason and time for any add-on.
• A supporting diagnosis code, as specific as the record allows.

**On the claim**
• Rendering NPI and taxonomy for the LCSW; billing NPI for the group.
• Correct place of service. For Medicare telehealth: POS 02 or 10, modifier 95 (93 for audio-only when allowed).
• Check NCCI edits and unit limits; file within the timely filing limit.

**After payment**
• Compare each payment to the contracted rate and appeal underpayments.
• Track denials by reason code and fix the front-end cause.

visual.sub: Most lost money is a front-end miss

cards.title: What We Could Not Confirm
cards.content:
• **Psychological testing (96130 and related codes)** for a California LCSW: sources disagree.
• **Partnership HealthPlan's LCSW code list and rates**, and exactly which codes go to the county.
• **Any commercial payer's covered codes, rates and prior authorization rules**: these come only from your contracts and that payer's policies.
• **Current Medicare telehealth rules for mental health** (such as any in-person visit requirement): these have changed several times. Check CMS's current guidance.
• **The 2023–2025 Medicare code additions** come from CMS and NASW summaries, not the Federal Register rule text itself.

boxes.b: Code lists and rates come from contracts.

cards.title: Key Takeaways and Sources
cards.content:
• Taxonomy **1041C0700X** is national; **specialty code 80** is Medicare's label for a clinical social worker.
• Medicare pays an LCSW **75%** of the fee schedule, and assignment is required.
• No payer hands you one complete list: check the code books, your state scope, and each payer's rules.
• Time decides psychotherapy codes: 90832 = 16–37, 90834 = 38–52, 90837 = 53+ minutes.
• LCSWs cannot bill E/M visits, 90792, E/M psychotherapy add-ons, or medication management.

**Sources:** CMS Medicare Benefit Policy Manual, Ch. 15 §170; CMS Medicare Claims Processing Manual, Ch. 12 §150; NUCC taxonomy code set; AMA CPT codebook (time ranges and add-on rules); NASW 2024 fee schedule highlights and 2025 safety-planning guidance; CMS MLN Behavioral Health Integration Services (2025); Partnership HealthPlan policy CLPM-28.
